label: Lead ID
description: System-generated reference for the pursuit, e.g. LEAD-00118.
use_case: Quoted in reviews, on quotes and in the audit trail so a deal can be discussed unambiguously.

label: Opportunity Name
description: Human-readable deal name in the format [Project Name] — [Client].
use_case: §7.1 mandates the format so pipeline lists are scannable without opening records.

label: Region
description: Broad operating region of the pursuit — MEA, APAC, India or Americas.
use_case: PROTOTYPE REGISTER EDIT, added beside Opportunity Name in STAGE 0 — CONNECT. Read through to Opportunities and Deals — see spec/module_split.json read_through.fields. Renamed from Country and unified with accounts.region onto the same picklist — see spec/extensions.json open_questions.

label: End Client
lookup_filter: Account Type must include End Client
values_note: Account Type must include End Client
description: The organisation that owns and operates the asset being instrumented.
use_case: §7.1 separates the asset owner from the contracting party; drives account penetration reporting.

label: Customer (Partner / SI)
lookup_filter: Account Type must include Partner / SI
values_note: Account Type must include Partner / SI
description: The partner or systems integrator bringing the opportunity and usually holding the contract.
use_case: §6.1 — most MEA pipeline is partner-led; this is who Astrikos actually invoices.

label: BD Owner
description: The BD person accountable for the pursuit.
use_case: §7.1 — every opportunity needs one accountable owner for pipeline reporting.

label: Primary Contact
description: The person at the client this pursuit is being run through.
use_case: Stage 0 is Connect — the whole stage is about establishing a named contact, and until now the lead recorded the ARK owner but not the client counterpart. Entry criterion E1.1 reads "Contact confirmed and meeting scheduled".

label: Deal Source
description: How the opportunity arrived: partner, direct or BD-generated.
use_case: §6.5 — management tracks direct versus partner pipeline mix; feeds the ≥70% partner contribution KPI.

label: Opportunity Type
description: Whether this is a new logo, an expansion or a renewal.
use_case: §7.1 — tracks land-and-expand momentum and separates new business from growth.

label: Partner Deal Registration
description: Link to the registration record that grants the partner exclusivity.
use_case: §6.2 — proves who found the deal when two partners claim the same client and project.

label: Segment
description: Top-level market segment for the opportunity.
use_case: §7.1 — aligns pipeline to the business plan's segment strategy.

label: Theme
description: The ROB theme this pursuit sits under — smart cities, energy, buildings, and so on.
use_case: PROTOTYPE REGISTER EDIT, added at review beside Segment in STAGE 0 — CONNECT, normalised from the ROB sheet's raw theme values. Read through to Opportunities and Deals. Segment stays alongside it — the two overlap and the register pass must decide whether both survive, see Spec Health.

label: S!aP Solution Suite
lookup_filter: Suite Type must be Primary suite
values_note: Suite Type must be Primary suite
description: The primary platform entry point being sold.
use_case: §2.2 — every opportunity must map to a primary suite; anchors the platform story.

label: Lead Stage
description: Where the opportunity sits in the ten-stage pipeline, 0 to 7 on a Lead.
use_case: §3.1 — drives probability, forecasting and review prioritisation. A stale stage invalidates the pipeline.

label: Lead Status
description: Whether the pursuit is open, paused, lost or converted.
use_case: §7.2 — separates live pipeline from history without deleting records.

label: Probability (%)
values_note: Must sit in the band for the current stage
description: Likelihood of winning, expressed as a percentage.
use_case: §3.1 — must sit within the band for the current stage; overrides need justification.

label: Expected Close Month
description: The month the order is expected to book.
use_case: §7.1 — the basis of the rolling forecast; must be reviewed monthly.

label: Currency
description: The currency the client is quoted and billed in.
use_case: §10.2 — MEA deals are quoted locally but reported in USD.

label: FX Rate at Entry
description: The rate to USD captured at the moment of entry.
use_case: §10.2 — multi-year contracts carry FX exposure; stamping the rate keeps reporting stable.

label: Estimated Value
description: Indicative deal value before bid financials exist.
use_case: §7.1 — gives Stage 0-3 opportunities a value so early pipeline can be sized.

label: Is Primary Pursuit
description: Marks this as the counted record where the same project is chased through several partners.
use_case: §7.2 — duplicates must not inflate pipeline value; only primary pursuits roll up.

label: Parent Pursuit
description: Link from a secondary pursuit back to the primary record for the same project.
use_case: §7.2 — keeps the duplicate visible for partner reporting while excluding it from totals.

label: Parent Deal
description: Link from an expansion lead back to the delivered deal that generated it.
use_case: §7.2 — the lineage that makes Platform Expansion Revenue % computable.

label: Incremental Value
description: Additional revenue expected from an expansion beyond the original deal.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 9 — sizes the expansion pipeline separately from new business.

label: Contracting Party
values_note: Customer (Partner / SI) where Deal Source = Partner-sourced, otherwise End Client
description: Derived: the partner on a partner-led deal, the end client on a direct one.
use_case: §6.1 — removes the Deal Source branch from invoicing, quoting and award handling.
computed_formula: Customer (Partner / SI) where Deal Source = Partner-sourced, otherwise End Client

label: Remarks / Notes
description: Running narrative of calls, decisions and context.
use_case: §7.1 — minimum one update per month; the qualitative record behind the numbers.

label: Lighthouse Project
description: Flagged as a lighthouse/reference-account pursuit — set once, read through the chain.
use_case: PROTOTYPE REGISTER EDIT, added at review. Identity, set once at Stage 0 and never re-derived — read through to Opportunities and Deals like Country and Theme.

label: Gorilla Flag
description: Flagged as a Gorilla-tier pursuit — set once, read through the chain.
use_case: PROTOTYPE REGISTER EDIT, added at review. Identity, set once at Stage 0 and never re-derived — read through to Opportunities and Deals like Country and Theme.

label: Demo Agreed
description: Confirms the client has agreed to see a platform demonstration.
use_case: Exit criterion X0.2 — the event that lets Stage 0 close.

label: Demo Scheduled Date
description: The date the demonstration is booked for.
use_case: Entry criterion E1.1 — a demo cannot be a stage until it is actually scheduled.

label: Demo Date
description: The date the demonstration was delivered.
use_case: Measures the gap between first contact and first demo.

label: Suite Demonstrated
description: Which S!aP suite was actually shown.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 1 — recorded because the suite shown is not always the suite eventually sold.

label: Demo Attendees
description: The client and partner people who attended, with their roles.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 1 — a demo attended only by junior technical staff is a warning sign.

label: Interest Level
description: Qualitative read on client interest after the demo.
use_case: Exit criterion X1.1 — the judgement that justifies investing in a POC.

label: Agreed Next Step
description: What both sides agreed happens next.
use_case: Exit criterion X1.1 — an interested client with no agreed next step is not progress.

label: Data / Site Access Confirmation Document
description: Written confirmation from the client that data and site access will be granted for the pilot.
use_case: Entry criterion E2.1 requires data or site access confirmed IN WRITING before Stage 2, and gate G1 POC Brief checks the same thing. Captured at the moment the POC is agreed, while the client is still in the room, rather than chased later.

label: Pilot Commercial Model
description: Whether the client pays for the pilot.
use_case: A free pilot and a paid pilot are different commitments. Recorded at scoping so the POC brief and any quote start from an agreed basis.

label: Pilot Fee
description: What the client pays for the pilot, in the lead currency.
use_case: Paid pilots are revenue and have to be quoted, invoiced and reported like any other one-time charge.

label: Client Feedback
description: What resonated, what did not, and questions raised.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 1 — feeds the Product Team debrief and future demo improvement.

label: Competitors Mentioned
values_note: Free text. Was typed multiselect with no value set behind it in the register.
description: Competitor products the client referenced during the demo.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 1 — the earliest competitive intelligence available on the deal.

label: Feature Gaps Logged
description: Capability gaps surfaced during the demo.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 1 — the product feedback loop; each gap is a roadmap candidate.

label: Demo Debrief Notes
description: What the Product Team and BD concluded when they debriefed after the demo.
use_case: Exit criterion X1.2 — replaces Demo Debrief Completed Date. A date proved a meeting happened; the notes are what the meeting was for, and they capture competitive mentions and feature gaps while they are fresh.

label: Demo Completed
description: Confirms Demo is completed
use_case: Exit criterion X0.2 — the event that lets Stage 1 close.

label: Secondary S!aP Suites
description: Additional suites identified as expansion candidates.
use_case: §7.1 — the foundation of platform upsell tracking; usually surfaced during a POC.

label: POC Record
description: Link to the POC engagement, where all pilot detail lives.
use_case: Annexure A — the POC is a managed engagement, not a field on the lead.

label: POC Brief Gate
description: Link to gate G1, which must pass before the POC can start.
use_case: Annexure A.1 — no POC starts without a signed brief.

label: Consultant / Specifier
description: The engineering consultant shaping the client's specification.
use_case: §7.1 — critical at Stages 3-5; often controls the specification language.

label: Sales Owner
description: The person holding commercial accountability from Stage 3.
use_case: §1.3 — Sales takes deal ownership at Prescription; today this resolves to the CEO.

label: Presales Owner
description: The person owning technical bid execution.
use_case: §9.3 — Presales joins at Stage 3 and owns the bid from Stage 4.

label: Client Phase
description: Whether the client is in solution design, budgeting, or neither.
use_case: Entry criterion E3.1 — a lead can enter Prescription without a POC if the client is already designing.

label: Project Team Access Confirmed
description: Confirms access to the client project team, PMO or consultant.
use_case: Entry criterion E3.2 — without access you cannot influence the specification.

label: Budget Estimate
description: The client's indicative budget for the project.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 3 — sizes the opportunity before bid financials exist.

label: Budget Confirmed
description: Confirms the budget is real and allocated, not indicative.
use_case: Exit criterion X3.2 — deliberately distinct from the estimate; an unfunded project is not a bid.

label: Probable Award Date
description: When the client expects to award the contract.
use_case: §4.2 item 1.2 — required at qualification; drives forecast timing.

label: Pre-Bid Alliance Partner
description: The partner Astrikos will bid alongside on this specific opportunity.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 3 — deliberately separate from Customer; the sourcing partner is not always the bidding partner.

label: Alliance Structure
description: Whether Astrikos is prime, the partner is prime, or Astrikos is a sub.
use_case: §6.1 — determines what TCV means, who issues the PO, and who carries payment risk.

label: PBAA Signed Date
description: When the Pre-Bid Alliance Agreement was executed.
use_case: Entry criterion E4.3 — bidding together on a handshake creates margin disputes at award.

label: CTB Gate
description: Link to gate G2, the Commit to Bid assessment.
use_case: §4.1 — no bid may proceed to Stage 4 without an approved CTB.

label: CTB Approval Status
description: The outcome of the Commit to Bid review.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 3 — records approvals, conditional approvals, deferrals and no-bids alike.

label: CTB Approval Date
description: When the CTB decision was taken.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 3 — evidences that the gate ran before the bid, not after.

label: Total Project Value
description: The whole engagement value where Astrikos is a subcontractor.
use_case: §6.1 — context for share of wallet; deliberately excluded from all pipeline totals.

label: RFP Type
description: Whether the client issued an RFP, RFI, tender or EOI.
use_case: Entry criterion E4.1 — an RFI is not a bid and should not carry the same probability.

label: RFP Received Date
description: When the formal request arrived.
use_case: Entry criterion E4.1 — starts the bid clock and the response window.

label: RFP Document
description: The tender document itself.
use_case: §4.2 item 2.2 — all tender documents must be received and distributed to the bid team.

label: Submission Deadline
description: The client's deadline for bid submission.
use_case: Exit criterion X4.1 — a late bid is a lost bid regardless of quality.

label: ARR (Annual Recurring)
description: Recurring revenue per year: subscription licence, or support and maintenance on a perpetual deal.
use_case: §7.1 — the compounding revenue line and its own KPI.

label: One-Time Revenue
description: Implementation, integration, configuration and training fees.
use_case: §7.1 — separated from licence so services margin can be seen independently.

label: 3rd-Party One-Time
description: Hardware and one-off OEM licences resold through the Astrikos contract, paid once.
use_case: §8.1 — must never be multiplied by contract years; doing so overstates TCV badly on hardware-heavy deals.

label: 3rd-Party Recurring (per year)
description: OEM subscriptions and annual passthrough licences resold each year.
use_case: §8.1 — genuinely recurring, so this is the only third-party line the contract term multiplies.

label: Contract Years
description: The contract term in years.
use_case: §7.1 — multiplies the recurring lines in the TCV calculation.

label: Total Value (TCV)
values_note: (ARR × Years) + Perpetual Licence Fee + One-Time + 3rd-Party One-Time + (3rd-Party Recurring × Years)
description: Computed total contract value across the full term.
use_case: §7.1 — the single number used for pipeline value, forecasting and threshold checks.
computed_formula: (ARR × Years) + Perpetual Licence Fee + One-Time + 3rd-Party One-Time + (3rd-Party Recurring × Years)

label: Gross Margin %
values_note: (((ARR × Contract Years) + Perpetual Licence Fee + One-Time Revenue) - Services & Implementation Cost) / ((ARR × Contract Years) + Perpetual Licence Fee + One-Time Revenue). Excludes third-party content.
description: Computed margin on Astrikos software and services, excluding third-party content.
use_case: §8.2 — minimum 45%; below that requires CEO and CFO approval.
computed_formula: (((ARR × Contract Years) + Perpetual Licence Fee + One-Time Revenue) - Services & Implementation Cost) / ((ARR × Contract Years) + Perpetual Licence Fee + One-Time Revenue)

label: Competitors Noticed
values_note: Free text. Was typed multiselect with no value set behind it in the register.
description: The competitors bidding against Astrikos.
use_case: §7.1 — feeds standing assessment and the win/loss library.

label: Bid Record
description: Link to the bid, which carries the 32-item checklist and TBE log.
use_case: §4.2 — a re-tender creates a second bid against the same lead.

label: Bid Submission Date
description: When the bid was actually submitted.
use_case: Exit criterion X4.1 — compared against the deadline to prove compliance.

label: Submitted On Time
description: Computed: whether submission met the deadline.
use_case: Exit criterion X4.1 — an objective compliance check rather than a claim.

label: Debrief Requested Date
description: When a post-submission debrief was requested from the client.
use_case: Exit criterion X4.3 — debriefs are the cheapest competitive intelligence available.

label: Platform Licence List Price
description: The undiscounted catalogue price of the platform licence.
use_case: §8.1 — without a list price a licence discount cannot be detected, and the licence is where the value is.

label: Licence Discount %
description: Computed discount against list on the platform licence.
use_case: §8.1 — never discount the platform licence without CEO approval; any non-zero value routes for approval.

label: Services & Implementation Cost
description: Internal cost of delivering the services scope.
use_case: §7.1 — gross margin cannot be computed without cost; previously margin was asserted, not calculated.

label: Third-Party Cost
description: Buy price of the hardware and OEM licences being resold.
use_case: §8.1 — exposes the real markup on pass-through content.

label: Total Cost
description: Computed sum of services and third-party cost.
use_case: §7.1 — the denominator behind the gross margin figure.

label: Third-Party % of TCV
description: Computed share of the contract that is pass-through content.
use_case: §4.1 CTB-04 and §8.2 — the 40% ceiling had no number behind it before this field.

label: Cost Model (RCM) Document
description: The Risk and Cost Model behind the margin figure.
use_case: §4.2 item 4.5 — makes the margin auditable rather than a number someone typed.

label: Licence Model
description: Whether the platform is sold as a subscription or a perpetual licence.
use_case: §8.1 — changes which revenue fields apply and how the discount check is calculated.

label: Perpetual Licence Fee
description: One-time platform licence fee on a perpetual deal.
use_case: §8.1 — keeps the licence line visible instead of hidden inside one-time services revenue.

label: Client Tender Reference
description: The client's own RFP or tender number.
use_case: Printed on the quote as Your Ref so the document is traceable in both organisations.

label: Primary Quote
description: The quote whose figures feed the lead's revenue fields.
use_case: §9.4 — BAFO and value engineering mean several quotes per lead; exactly one is primary.

label: Bid Receipt Confirmed Date
description: When the client confirmed receipt of the bid.
use_case: Entry criterion E5.1 — a submitted bid is not an evaluated bid until receipt is acknowledged.

label: First TBE Received Date
description: When the first technical evaluation query arrived.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 5 — marks the real start of evaluation and the SLA clock.

label: Technical Standing
description: Assessment of competitive position: leading, equal or trailing.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 5 — re-assessed each round; trailing status escalates to the CEO.

label: Technical Approval Status
description: Whether technical approval or approved-vendor status has been achieved.
use_case: Exit criterion X5.2 — the gate between technical and commercial evaluation.

label: Technical Approval Date
description: When technical approval was received.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 5 — measures technical evaluation cycle time.

label: Commercial Proposal Submitted Date
description: When the commercial proposal went to client procurement.
use_case: Entry criterion E6.2 — commercial evaluation begins when procurement has the numbers.

label: Final Negotiated Value
description: The agreed contract value after negotiation.
use_case: Exit criterion X6.1 — compared against the bid value to measure concession.

label: Contract Review Status
description: Progress of the internal contract review.
use_case: Exit criterion X6.2 — the review that catches red lines before signature.

label: Contract Review Sign-Off Date
description: When the contract review was signed off.
use_case: §4.2 item 4.1 — CMG sign-off is mandatory before closure.

label: Contract Review Sign-Off By
description: Who approved the contract review.
use_case: §4.2 item 4.1 — accountability for the terms accepted.

label: Commercial Gate
description: Link to gate G3, covering thresholds and contract red lines.
use_case: §8.2 and §8.4 — the last governance check before an order is booked.

label: Award Type
description: The form the award took: LOI, verbal, PO or signed contract.
use_case: Exit criterion X6.3 — a verbal award is not a contract and should be visible as such.

label: LOI Received Date
description: When the letter of intent arrived.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 6 — confirmed with CEO and Finance immediately on receipt.

label: Agreed Advance %
description: The advance payment percentage agreed with the client.
use_case: §8.2 — policy minimum is 10%; below that needs Commercial Head approval, above 15% triggers an ABG.

label: Agreed Credit Period (days)
description: Days from invoice to payment as agreed.
use_case: §8.2 — 30 days is standard; beyond 60 requires CFO approval.

label: Agreed Liability Cap %
description: The liability cap accepted in the contract.
use_case: §8.4 red line RL-01 — unlimited liability can end the company on a single project.

label: Agreed LD Cap %
description: The liquidated damages cap accepted.
use_case: §8.4 red line RL-02 — damages above 10% can exceed the profit on the deal.

label: Pay-When-Paid
description: Flags that payment depends on the prime being paid first.
use_case: §10.2 — a real cash-flow exposure on subcontracts that is otherwise invisible.

label: PO Number
description: The purchase order reference received.
use_case: Entry criterion E7.1 — on a subcontract this comes from the partner, not the end client.

label: Contract Signed Date
description: When the contract was executed.
use_case: Entry criterion E7.1 — either a PO or a signed contract is required to enter Close.

label: Payment Schedule Confirmed
description: Confirms the milestone schedule is agreed.
use_case: Entry criterion E7.2 — an award without agreed payment timing is not closeable.

label: Payment Milestones
description: The eight standard milestones with their percentages and triggers.
use_case: §8.3 — 40% sits behind delivery alone, so milestone timing is a cash-flow control.

label: Milestone — Planned Date
description: Planned date for each payment milestone.
use_case: §8.2 — enables the rule that delivery must be no more than 60 days from FAT.

label: Milestone — Actual Date
description: Actual achievement date for the milestone.
use_case: §8.3 — measures slippage against plan.

label: Milestone — Invoice Date
description: When the milestone was invoiced.
use_case: §4.2 item 4.3 — the basis of the pre-delivery cash flow statement.

label: Milestone — Payment Received Date
description: When payment actually arrived.
use_case: §8.2 — credit period is measured from invoice to this date.

label: Probability Override Justification
description: Reason for setting probability outside the stage band.
use_case: §3.1 — overrides are permitted but must be justified in writing.

label: Stage Skip Reason
description: Why the lead jumped forward past one or more stages.
use_case: §3.2 — skipping is legal; unexplained skipping is not.

label: Stage Reversal Reason
description: Why the lead moved backwards.
use_case: §3.2 — a reissued tender is the common case; the reason keeps the history honest.

label: Closed Lost Reason Code
description: Structured reason the pursuit was lost.
use_case: §7.2 and §11.2 — drives win/loss analysis; cannot be added retrospectively.

label: On Hold Reason
description: Why the pursuit is paused rather than closed.
use_case: §7.2 — distinguishes a paused deal from a dead one in the forecast.

label: Close Date Pushback Count
description: Computed count of close-date deferrals.
use_case: §7.2 — a second pushback triggers management discussion and re-qualification.

label: Days in Current Stage
description: Computed age in the current stage.
use_case: §3.1 — more than 60 days requires a documented reason and escalation.

label: Days Since Last Update
description: Computed days since the record last changed.
use_case: §7.2 — 30 days marks the lead stale and puts it in the weekly review queue.

label: Created By
description: User who created the record.
use_case: Audit — establishes provenance.

label: Created Date
description: When the record was created.
use_case: Audit — the start of the pursuit clock.

label: Modified By
description: User who last changed the record.
use_case: Audit — accountability for the current state.

label: Modified Date
description: When the record last changed.
use_case: §7.2 — the basis of the stale-lead calculation.

label: Deal ID
description: System-generated reference for the won order, e.g. DEAL-00031.
use_case: Separates the order book from the pursuit pipeline.

label: Deal Name
description: Human-readable name of the delivered engagement.
use_case: Carried from the lead so the same project is recognisable after conversion.

label: Parent Lead
description: Permanent link back to the pursuit that won this deal.
use_case: §7.2 — preserves the full bid history without duplicating it onto the deal.

label: End Client
description: The organisation operating the delivered platform.
use_case: §7.1 — CSAT and references come from here even when a partner holds the contract.

label: Customer (Partner / SI)
description: The contracting party being invoiced.
use_case: §6.1 — on a subcontract this is the partner, not the end client.

label: Deal Stage
description: Whether the deal is in project success, expansion or closed.
use_case: §3.1 — Stages 8 and 9 live on the deal, not the lead.

label: Delivery PM
description: The person accountable for delivery execution.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 7 — assigned at booking so handover has a named recipient.

label: Order Booked
description: Confirms the order has been booked in CRM and ERP.
use_case: Exit criterion X7.1 — the moment pipeline becomes revenue.

label: Booking Date
description: When the order was booked.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 7 — the date used for bookings-versus-target reporting.

label: ERP Reference
description: The booking reference in the finance system.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 7 — links the CRM record to the financial record.

label: PO / LOI Reference
description: The client or partner award document reference.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 7 — the commercial authority for the work.

label: Project Code
description: Internal project identifier assigned at booking.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 7 — the key Delivery and Finance use for the engagement.

label: Contract Value
description: Final contract value at booking.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 7 — the basis of revenue recognition and margin reporting.

label: ARR (Annual Recurring)
description: Recurring revenue carried forward from the lead.
use_case: §11.1 — feeds the ARR KPI once booked.

label: One-Time Revenue
description: One-time revenue carried forward from the lead.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 7 — the ARR versus one-time split must be confirmed at booking.

label: 3rd-Party One-Time
description: One-off third-party content carried forward from the lead.
use_case: §8.1 — tracked separately through delivery because it carries no margin.

label: 3rd-Party Recurring (per year)
description: Recurring third-party content carried forward from the lead.
use_case: §8.1 — renews annually alongside the platform subscription.

label: Contract Years
description: Contract term carried forward from the lead.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 7 — drives renewal timing and expiry alerts.

label: PSP Completed Date
description: When the Project Strategy Paper was completed.
use_case: Exit criterion X7.2 — the document that guides Delivery.

label: Handover Pack Delivered Date
description: When the Technical Handover Pack was presented to Delivery.
use_case: §9.3 — Stage 7 cannot close without it; carries every commitment made during the bid.

label: Kickoff Meeting Date
description: When the delivery kickoff is scheduled.
use_case: Exit criterion X7.3 — ensures a clean transition rather than a silent handover.

label: Cash Flow Sign-Off Date
description: When Finance approved the pre-delivery cash flow.
use_case: §4.2 item 4.3 — confirms the project can be funded to first payment.

label: Resource Plan Sign-Off Date
description: When Delivery approved the resource plan.
use_case: §4.2 item 4.4 — confirms the team exists before the work is promised.

label: Bid Commitments Register
description: Every commitment made during bid and negotiation.
use_case: §9.3 — commitments made in TBE responses become delivery obligations.

label: Guarantee — Type
description: Whether the instrument is an advance or performance guarantee.
use_case: §8.2 — ABG and PBG carry different triggers and different policy ceilings.

label: Guarantee — Value
description: Face value of the bank guarantee.
use_case: §8.2 — consumes banking facility and therefore capacity to bid elsewhere.

label: Guarantee — % of Contract Value
description: Computed guarantee value as a share of the contract.
use_case: §8.2 — PBG is capped at 10%; above that requires CEO approval.

label: Guarantee — Issue Date
description: When the guarantee was issued.
use_case: §8.2 — starts the validity clock.

label: Guarantee — Expiry Date
description: When the guarantee lapses or must be released.
use_case: §8.2 — maximum 12 months; an unreleased guarantee quietly ties up capital for years.

label: Guarantee — Issuing Bank
description: The bank that issued the instrument.
use_case: §8.2 — facilities are bank-specific and must be managed per relationship.

label: Guarantee — Status
description: Lifecycle state from requested through to released or called.
use_case: §8.2 — release frees the facility for the next bid.

label: Commissioning Date
description: When the system was commissioned on site.
use_case: Entry criterion E8.1 — the start of Project Success.

label: T&C Sign-Off Date
description: When the client signed the testing and commissioning certificate.
use_case: Entry criterion E8.1 and §8.3 — triggers the T&C payment milestone.

label: Go-Live Date
description: When the platform went live in production.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 8 — anchors the 30 and 90-day re-engagement tasks.

label: Warranty Start Date
description: When the warranty or support period began.
use_case: Entry criterion E8.2 — support obligations begin here.

use_case: Pricing tool — the master price; all regional prices derive from it.

label: Price Book Version
description: Which edition of the price book this row belongs to.
use_case: Lets a historical quote keep the price that applied when it was issued.

label: Is Derived
description: Computed: the Unlimited tier is XXL multiplied by 1.3.
use_case: Pricing tool — the derivation is stated in the price list rather than hand-entered.

label: Size Code
description: XS through to Unlimited.
use_case: Sizing guide — size drives price, base users and hardware, so it is the single most consequential quote input.

label: Managed Assets Cap
values_note: Up to 50 · Up to 500 · Up to 5,000 · No cap
description: The asset ceiling for this size, e.g. up to 5,000.
use_case: Sizing guide — assets covers IoT, OT, IT and ET endpoints under management.

label: Typical Deployment
values_note: Pilot / single facility · Mega smart city
description: What a deployment of this size looks like in practice.
use_case: Sizing guide — helps a seller pick the right size without a technical assessment.

label: Subsystem Types
description: How many distinct subsystem types this size assumes.
use_case: Sizing guide — a sanity check on integration complexity.

label: Base Users Included
description: Users included at this size before user packs are added.
use_case: Users price list — additional users are only charged above this included allowance.

label: Sort Order
description: Display sequence for the category.
use_case: Keeps the services section of the quote in delivery order.

label: Region Code
description: The pricing geography, e.g. UAE AED or India INR.
use_case: FX sheet — pricing varies by region as well as by currency.

label: Currency
description: The currency the region quotes in.
use_case: FX sheet — determines the display format on the quote.

label: Region Pricing %
description: Regional price level as a percentage of USA pricing.
use_case: FX sheet — GCC is 100%, ASEAN 56%, India 31%; a deliberate market-rate policy, not a discount.

label: FX Rate (local per USD)
description: Exchange rate from USD into the local currency.
use_case: FX sheet — combined with the region percentage to convert the master price.

label: Effective Multiplier
description: Computed: region percentage multiplied by FX rate.
use_case: FX sheet — the single number applied to every list price on the quote.

label: Display Format
description: How amounts are rendered for this region.
use_case: FX sheet — a quote showing the wrong currency symbol undermines credibility.

label: Rate Effective Date
description: When this rate came into force.
use_case: §10.2 — FX exposure on multi-year contracts is a logged commercial risk.

label: Perpetual Multiplier
description: Factor converting an annual price into a perpetual licence fee.
use_case: FX sheet — currently 3.2 times the annual subscription price.

label: Support Perpetual AMC Uplift
description: Uplift applied to support pricing on perpetual deals.
use_case: FX sheet — currently 1.3; perpetual clients pay more for support because there is no subscription.

label: User Blended Rate (USD/user/yr)
description: Blended annual rate per user.
use_case: FX sheet — currently 320; used to sanity-check user pack pricing.

label: Unlimited Tier Multiplier
description: Factor applied to XXL to derive the Unlimited price.
use_case: Price lists — currently 1.3 across modules, segments and add-ons.

label: Onsite Premium Multiplier
description: Uplift applied to offsite service rates when work is onsite.
use_case: Rate card — currently 1.5; onsite delivery costs materially more.

label: Segment Annual Update %
values_note: Annual library updates as % of one-time library price
description: Annual library update charge as a percentage of the one-time library price.
use_case: Segments price list — libraries are bought once and optionally maintained annually.

label: Level
description: Service delivery grade, L1 to L4.
use_case: Rate card — the four levels from associate engineer to subject matter expert.

label: Role
values_note: Associate Dev · Mid/Senior Dev · Technical Architect · Subject Matter Expert
description: The role description for the level.
use_case: Rate card — makes the rate defensible to a client who asks what they are paying for.

label: Rate per Hour — Offsite
description: Hourly rate for remote delivery.
use_case: Rate card — the base rate from which all service pricing derives.

label: Rate per Day — Offsite
description: Daily rate for remote delivery, based on an eight-hour day.
use_case: Rate card — services are normally quoted in days, not hours.

label: Rate per Hour — Onsite
description: Computed offsite hourly rate with the onsite premium applied.
use_case: Rate card — prevents onsite work being quoted at offsite rates by mistake.

label: Rate per Day — Onsite
description: Computed offsite daily rate with the onsite premium applied.
use_case: Rate card — the figure that actually appears on most service lines.

label: Service Category
description: One of the five standard professional services categories.
use_case: Rate card — project management, discovery, development, integration, and commissioning.

label: Sort Order
description: Display sequence for the category.
use_case: Keeps the services section of the quote in delivery order.

label: Tier
description: Support level: basic, standard, premium or 24x7 mission critical.
use_case: Support price list — four tiers with defined coverage and response times.

label: Coverage
values_note: Email only 8x5 next-business-day · Email + phone 24x7 1h response
description: What the tier includes: channels, hours and response time.
use_case: Support price list — the commitment being sold, and later the obligation being delivered.

label: % of Annual Licence
description: Support price as a percentage of the annual licence value.
use_case: Support price list — 18, 22, 28 or 35 percent; support scales with the licence rather than being priced separately.

label: Quote ID
description: System reference for the quote, e.g. QT-00087.
use_case: §9.4 — the reference printed as Our Ref and quoted back by the client.

label: Revision
description: Revision marker, R0, R1, R2.
use_case: §9.4 — a sent quote is immutable; a change creates the next revision.

label: Lead
description: The opportunity this quote belongs to.
use_case: The proof that these line items belong to this pursuit, and the link that makes rollups possible.

label: Quote Type
description: Initial, revised, value-engineered alternative or BAFO.
use_case: §9.4 — value engineering requires scoped-down alternatives with documented impact.

label: Status
description: Draft through to accepted, rejected, superseded or expired.
use_case: §9.4 — the quote and its lines freeze at Sent so what was issued can always be reproduced.

label: Customer Name
description: The organisation the quote is addressed to.
use_case: Pricing tool — printed on the quote header.

label: Project / Site
description: The specific project or site being quoted.
use_case: Pricing tool — one client may run several concurrent projects.

label: Quote Date
description: The date of issue.
use_case: Pricing tool — starts the validity clock.

label: Prepared By
description: Who produced the quote.
use_case: Pricing tool — accountability for the pricing presented.

label: Validity (days)
description: How long the quote remains open, default 60.
use_case: §9.4 — prevents an old price being accepted after costs have moved.

label: Valid Until
description: Computed expiry date.
use_case: §9.4 — drives the expired status and the follow-up prompt.

label: Our Ref
description: Computed quote reference including revision.
use_case: The reference the client quotes back; the anchor of the paper trail.

label: Your Ref (Client Tender Reference)
description: The client's own RFP or tender number.
use_case: Makes the quote traceable in the client's system as well as in ARK.

label: Bill To Account
description: The organisation being invoiced.
use_case: §6.1 — the partner on a partner-led deal, the end client on a direct one.

label: End Client
description: The organisation that will operate the platform.
use_case: §7.1 — shown alongside Bill To because on partner deals they differ.

label: Region / Currency
values_note: USA USD · UAE AED · India INR
description: The pricing geography for this quote.
use_case: Pricing tool — sets the effective multiplier applied to every list price.

label: Effective Multiplier
values_note: Snapshot of Region Pricing % x FX Rate
description: Snapshot of the region percentage multiplied by the FX rate.
use_case: Snapshotting protects the quote from later FX movement.
computed_formula: Snapshot of Region Pricing % x FX Rate

label: Licence Type
description: Subscription or perpetual.
use_case: §8.1 — perpetual prices at 3.2 times annual and changes which lines are one-time.

label: Subscription Years
values_note: Contract term used for TCV and TCO
description: Contract term used for TCV and TCO.
use_case: Pricing tool — multiplies the annual lines in the total contract value.

label: Deployment T-shirt Size
description: XS through Unlimited.
use_case: Pricing tool — the single input that sets the price of every module, segment and add-on line.

label: Total Users Required
description: Total named users the client needs.
use_case: Pricing tool — compared against the base allowance to size user packs.

label: Base Users Included
description: Computed users included with the chosen size.
use_case: Users price list — users are only charged above this allowance.

label: Additional Users Required
values_note: Total Users minus Base Users Included
description: Computed shortfall between total and included users.
use_case: Pricing tool — determines which user packs are added to the quote.
computed_formula: Total Users minus Base Users Included

label: Support Tier
description: The support level being quoted.
use_case: Support price list — priced as a percentage of the annual licence value.

label: Category
description: The discount category: modules, segments, users, add-ons, services or support.
use_case: Pricing tool — Astrikos discounts by category rather than per line.

label: Discount %
description: Discount applied across every line in that category.
use_case: §8.1 — any discount on the licence categories requires CEO approval.

label: Discount Approval
description: Link to the approval covering this discount.
use_case: §8.1 — never discount the platform licence without CEO approval.

label: Line No
description: Sequence number of the quote line.
use_case: Pricing tool — only lines with a quantity above zero appear on the issued quote.

label: Quote
description: The quote this line belongs to.
use_case: Parent link for the rollups.

label: Product
description: The catalogue item being quoted.
use_case: Links the line to the price book and its charge type.

label: SKU Code
description: Snapshot of the SKU code at time of quoting.
use_case: Snapshot so a later catalogue rename cannot rewrite an issued quote.

label: Item Name
description: Snapshot of the item name.
use_case: Snapshot for the same reason as the code.

label: Description
description: Snapshot of the item description, editable per quote.
use_case: Lets a seller tailor wording without altering the catalogue.

label: Line Category
description: Which discount category this line belongs to.
use_case: Pricing tool — determines which category discount applies and which subtotal it feeds.

label: Line Charge Type
description: Whether this line is annual or one-time.
use_case: Pricing tool — the field that decides whether the amount is multiplied by contract years.

label: Line Size
description: The T-shirt size used to price this line.
use_case: Pricing tool — normally the deployment size, but can differ where a module is scoped differently.

label: Include
description: Whether the item is included in this quote.
use_case: Pricing tool — modules are chosen by inclusion rather than quantity.

label: Annual Updates
description: Whether the optional annual library update is taken.
use_case: Segments price list — converts a one-time library into a line with a recurring component.

label: Quantity
description: Number of units, counted in the item's unit of measure.
use_case: Pricing tool — a quantity of 4 means four user packs or four hundred cameras depending on the unit.

label: Unit List Price (snapshot)
description: The list price captured at the moment of quoting.
use_case: Never read live, or repricing the catalogue would silently rewrite historical margin.

label: Gross Line
description: Computed quantity multiplied by unit list price.
use_case: The pre-discount value of the line.

label: Discount % Applied
description: Computed discount inherited from the line's category.
use_case: Pricing tool — discounting is set per category and applied down to the lines.

label: Net Line Total
description: Computed line value after discount.
use_case: The number that feeds the subtotals and ultimately the lead's revenue fields.

label: Service Level
description: L1 to L4, for service lines only.
use_case: Rate card — determines the day rate applied.

label: Service Delivery Mode
description: Offsite or onsite, for service lines only.
use_case: Rate card — onsite carries a 1.5 times premium.

label: Service Days
description: Number of days quoted at this level and mode.
use_case: Rate card — services are quoted in days against the five service categories.

label: Line Notes
description: Free text specific to this line.
use_case: Captures scope caveats that belong to one item rather than the whole quote.

label: Subtotal — Modules
description: Rollup of all module lines.
use_case: Pricing tool — shown on the quote so the client can see platform cost separately.

label: Subtotal — Segment Libraries
description: Rollup of all segment library lines.
use_case: Pricing tool — libraries are one-time, so this is a capital line for the client.

label: Subtotal — Users
description: Rollup of all user pack lines.
use_case: Pricing tool — scales with headcount rather than deployment size.

label: Subtotal — Add-Ons
description: Rollup of all add-on lines.
use_case: Pricing tool — the optional capability layer.

label: Subtotal — Services
description: Rollup of all professional services lines.
use_case: Pricing tool — the implementation effort priced from the rate card.

label: Subtotal — Support / AMC
description: Rollup of the support line.
use_case: Pricing tool — derived as a percentage of the annual licence value.

label: One-Time Cost
values_note: Sum of lines where Charge Type = One-Time
description: Rollup of every line whose charge type is one-time.
use_case: Pricing tool — perpetual licences, segment libraries and services; paid once.
computed_formula: Sum of lines where Charge Type = One-Time

label: Annual Recurring
values_note: Sum of lines where Charge Type = Annual
description: Rollup of every line whose charge type is annual.
use_case: Pricing tool — subscription, users, add-ons, updates and support; this is the ARR the deal generates.
computed_formula: Sum of lines where Charge Type = Annual

label: Year 1 Total
description: Computed one-time plus annual recurring.
use_case: Pricing tool — what the client actually pays in the first year.

label: Total Contract Value
description: Computed one-time plus annual multiplied by contract years.
use_case: The correct TCV formula: because each line is tagged one-time or annual, one-off hardware is never multiplied by the term.

label: 3-Year TCO
description: Computed total cost of ownership over three years.
use_case: Pricing tool — the standard comparison horizon in client evaluations.

label: 5-Year TCO
description: Computed total cost of ownership over five years.
use_case: Pricing tool — used where the client evaluates on a longer horizon.

label: Total Discount Value
description: Computed difference between gross and net totals.
use_case: §8.1 — makes the total concession visible in money, not just percentages.

label: Payment Terms
description: The milestone schedule offered.
use_case: §8.3 — defaults from the eight standard milestones.

label: Assumptions
description: What the pricing assumes.
use_case: §9.4 — assumptions that go unstated become disputes during delivery.

label: Exclusions
description: What is explicitly not included.
use_case: §9.3 — exclusions feed the technical handover pack and protect the delivery team.

label: Is Primary
description: Marks the quote whose figures feed the lead.
use_case: §7.2 — exactly one primary quote per lead, so revenue is never double counted.

label: Sent Date
description: When the quote was issued to the client.
use_case: §9.4 — the moment the quote and its lines become immutable.

label: Sent To
description: The client contact the quote was sent to.
use_case: Establishes who holds the offer and who to chase.

label: Quote PDF
description: The generated document, filed as register reference D23.
use_case: §9.4 — the artefact the client actually received, frozen with the quote.

label: Superseded By
description: The later revision that replaced this quote.
use_case: §9.4 — keeps the revision chain intact so a lost bid can be reconstructed.

label: Activity ID
description: System reference for the interaction, e.g. ACT-00913.
use_case: Stable key for the engagement record.

label: Subject
description: Short description of the interaction.
use_case: Makes the timeline scannable without opening each entry.

label: Activity Type
description: Call, meeting, email, note, demo, site visit, weekly review or QBR.
use_case: §7.2 — different interaction types carry different evidential weight for stage progression.

label: Related To
values_note: Lead · Deal · Account · Contact · Partner · POC · Bid
description: The record the document belongs to.
use_case: Documents attach to leads, deals, accounts, partners, POCs, bids or gates.

label: Activity Date
description: When the interaction happened.
use_case: §7.2 — the basis of the 30-day stale calculation and of stage-progression evidence.

label: Owner
description: Who at Astrikos conducted or logged the interaction.
use_case: Accountability for follow-up.

label: Attendees
description: Client and partner people present.
use_case: §3.2 Stage 1 — who attends a demo is itself a qualification signal.

label: Outcome
description: What was agreed or learned.
use_case: §7.2 — stage progression must be supported by documented evidence.

label: Next Action
description: The agreed next step.
use_case: §7.3 — the weekly BD sync runs on next actions.

label: Next Action Date
description: When the next step is due.
use_case: §7.3 — turns an intention into something trackable.

label: Document ID
description: System reference for the stored document.
use_case: Stable key linking CRM metadata to the file in SharePoint.

label: Document Name
description: Human-readable file name.
use_case: Findability.

label: Register Reference
values_note: D01 to D48 from the forms and documents register
description: Which of the 48 playbook documents this is, D01 to D48.
use_case: Ties every stored file to the forms and agreements register so gaps are visible.

label: Document Type
description: Internal governance, client-facing, client-issued, partner-facing, bank instrument or internal handover.
use_case: Controls handling and visibility; client-issued documents are evidence, internal ones are working papers.

label: Related To
values_note: Lead · Deal · Account · Partner · POC · Bid · Gate
description: The record the document belongs to.
use_case: Documents attach to leads, deals, accounts, partners, POCs, bids or gates.

label: Version
description: Document version identifier.
use_case: Prevents an old draft being mistaken for the issued version.

label: Signed
description: Whether the document has been executed.
use_case: Annexure A.1 — the POC brief and PBAA are only valid once signed.

label: Signed Date
description: When it was signed.
use_case: Evidence for gate checks that depend on signature.

label: Confidential
description: Restricts access to the document.
use_case: §14 — the playbook and its derivatives are confidential and internal.

label: Uploaded By
description: Who filed the document.
use_case: Audit trail.

label: Uploaded Date
description: When it was filed.
use_case: Audit trail; also shows how promptly evidence is captured.

label: User ID
description: System reference for the user account.
use_case: Stable key for ownership and approval routing.

label: Name
description: The user's name.
use_case: Displayed as record owner and approver.

label: Email
description: Their work email, matched to Entra ID.
use_case: Single sign-on identity and notification address.

label: Roles
description: Multi-select role assignment.
use_case: §1.3 — ARK assigns roles, not teams. Today one person holds every commercial role; in future the rows re-point without code changes.

label: Active
description: Whether the account is enabled.
use_case: Deactivates a leaver without deleting their history.

label: Stage Number
description: The stage this definition describes, 0 to 9.
use_case: §3.1 — the ten stages held as data rather than hardcoded.

label: Stage Name
description: The stage's name.
use_case: §3.1 — reproduced from the playbook so language stays consistent.

label: Probability Min / Max
description: The probability band for this stage.
use_case: §3.1 — probability must reflect the band; deviations require justification.

label: Owner Role
description: The role accountable at this stage.
use_case: §3.1 — BD owns 0 to 3, Sales 3 to 7, Delivery 8 and 9.

label: Bid Phase
description: Which of the four bid phases this stage sits in.
use_case: §4.2 — links the stage model to the bid checklist phases.

label: Applies To
description: Whether the stage belongs to Leads or Deals.
use_case: Stages 0 to 7 are Lead stages; 8 and 9 are Deal stages.

label: Module
description: Which module the field belongs to.
use_case: One metadata row exists per field across the whole system.

label: API Name
description: The immutable technical name of the field.
use_case: Renaming a label must never break a rule that references the field.

label: Label
description: What the user sees on screen.
use_case: Editable by an admin without any code change.

label: Field Type
description: The data type of the field.
use_case: Immutable once data exists; a type change is a migration, not a setting.

label: Section
description: Which group the field appears in on the form.
use_case: Drives the layout without hardcoding it in React.

label: Display Order
description: Position within the section.
use_case: Lets the form be reordered from configuration.

label: Capture at Stage
description: The stage at which the user is asked to fill the field.
use_case: §7.1 — fields become relevant progressively rather than all at once.

label: Requirement
description: Mandatory, conditional, advisory, optional, computed or system.
use_case: Determines whether an empty field blocks, warns or is ignored.

label: Condition
description: The expression that makes a conditional field mandatory.
use_case: Lets Perpetual Licence Fee be required only on perpetual deals.

label: Visibility Condition
description: The expression that controls whether the field is shown.
use_case: How partner fields disappear on a direct deal, without a code change.

label: Blocks Transition
description: Which stage move fails if the field is empty.
use_case: Turns the field register directly into the Phase 2 validation rule set.

label: Required On Skip
description: Whether the field is still required when its stage was skipped.
use_case: §3.2 — distinguishes stage-local fields, waived on a skip, from cumulative ones that are always needed.

label: Help Text
description: Guidance shown to the user at the field.
use_case: Reduces misinterpretation without training.

label: Is Core
description: Marks playbook-derived fields whose type and existence are locked.
use_case: Core fields can be relabelled but not deleted, because gates and computed columns depend on them.

label: Origin
description: Whether the field comes from the playbook, a gap fix or a later customisation.
use_case: Keeps traceability back to the source clause.

label: Stage
description: The stage this criterion applies to.
use_case: §3.2 — criteria are held per stage as configuration.

label: Criterion Type
description: Whether the criterion is checked on entry or on exit.
use_case: §3.2 — entry criteria are the only check that survives a stage skip.

label: Criterion Code
description: The criterion identifier, e.g. E4.1 or X3.2.
use_case: Gives every rule a stable reference for discussion and debugging.

label: Criterion Text
description: The criterion as written in the playbook.
use_case: Preserves the original wording so the rule can be audited against source.

label: Evaluation Type
description: Whether the criterion is evaluated automatically or attested by a person.
use_case: Roughly a fifth of criteria are genuine judgement calls and should not be forced into fields.

label: Source Field or Record
description: What the rule reads to decide.
use_case: Makes the dependency between rules and fields explicit.

label: Enforcement
description: Blocking, advisory or off.
use_case: The switch that lets enforcement be phased in criterion by criterion as adoption settles.

label: Playbook Reference
description: The clause the criterion derives from.
use_case: Traceability; also what to re-read when the playbook is revised.

label: Gate Type
description: Which of the three gates this definition configures.
use_case: POC Brief, CTB and Commercial.

label: Anchor Stage
description: The stage whose entry triggers the gate.
use_case: Gates anchor to the target stage's entry so a forward skip cannot bypass them.

label: Blocking Threshold
description: The deal value above which the gate blocks.
use_case: §4.1 — the playbook requires CTB on every bid; a threshold can relax that for small deals if the business chooses.

label: Threshold Parameter
description: Which commercial policy the row governs.
use_case: §8.2 — the eight thresholds from the approval matrix.

label: Policy Value
description: The policy limit for the parameter.
use_case: §8.2 — e.g. minimum 45 percent gross margin, maximum 40 percent third-party content.

label: Approver Role
description: Who must approve when the policy is breached.
use_case: §8.2 — CEO, CEO and CFO, CEO and Legal, Commercial Head or BD Manager.

label: Approval ID
description: System reference for an approval request.
use_case: Stable key for the decision record.

label: Approval Type
description: What is being approved.
use_case: §8.2 — CTB, margin, third-party, guarantees, credit, damages, liability, BAFO, contract review or red line.

label: Related Record
description: The lead, deal or quote the approval concerns.
use_case: Links the decision to the thing being decided.

label: Requested By
description: Who raised the approval request.
use_case: Half of the self-approval calculation.

label: Requested Date
description: When the request was raised.
use_case: Measures approval turnaround.

label: Approver
description: Who decided.
use_case: §8.2 — resolved from the approver role on the threshold.

label: Decision
description: Pending, approved, approved with conditions or rejected.
use_case: The outcome the gate or transition reads.

label: Decision Date
description: When the decision was made.
use_case: Evidence the approval preceded the commitment.

label: Self-Approval
description: Computed: requester and approver are the same person.
use_case: §1.3 — recorded honestly rather than hidden; disappears naturally as the team grows.

label: Comment
description: The reasoning behind the decision.
use_case: Turns an approval into a defensible record rather than a rubber stamp.

label: Record
description: The lead or deal that moved.
use_case: Every transition is logged against its record.

label: From Stage
description: The stage the record left.
use_case: Enables cycle-time and velocity analysis per stage.

label: To Stage
description: The stage the record entered.
use_case: Together with From Stage, reveals skips and reversals.

label: Transition Type
description: Advance, skip forward, move back, exit or conversion.
use_case: §3.2 — stages are states, so all five movements are legitimate and must be distinguishable.

label: Moved By
description: Who performed the transition.
use_case: Accountability for pipeline movement.

label: Moved At
description: When the transition happened.
use_case: The raw data behind days-in-stage and bid cycle time.

label: Reason
description: Why the record moved, mandatory on skips, reversals and exits.
use_case: §3.2 — skipping is legal; unexplained skipping is not.

label: Evidence Link
description: The proof behind the attestation.
use_case: A judgement with attached evidence is defensible; one without is an opinion.

label: Checks Passed
description: Snapshot of which validation checks passed.
use_case: Lets a past transition be explained without re-running the rules as they exist today.

label: Checks Failed
description: Snapshot of any advisory checks that failed but were accepted.
use_case: Advisory means it did not stop the move, not that it went unnoticed.

label: Criterion
description: The stage criterion being attested.
use_case: §3.2 — attestation covers criteria no system can evaluate.

label: Confirmed By
description: Who made the judgement.
use_case: Puts a name against a subjective call.

label: Confirmed Date
description: When the judgement was made.
use_case: Shows the assessment was current at the time of the transition.

label: Evidence Link
description: The proof behind the attestation.
use_case: A judgement with attached evidence is defensible; one without is an opinion.

label: Attestation Note
description: The reasoning for the judgement.
use_case: Explains why the criterion was considered met.

label: Audit — Record / Field
description: Which record and field changed.
use_case: §7.2 — field-level audit on stage, probability, money and approvals.

label: Audit — Old Value
description: The value before the change.
use_case: Enables reconstruction of any record's state at any past date.

label: Audit — New Value
description: The value after the change.
use_case: The other half of the change record.

label: Audit — Changed By
description: Who made the change.
use_case: Accountability, and the basis of any dispute resolution.

label: Audit — Changed At
description: When the change was made.
use_case: Chronology; an audit trail cannot be reconstructed later, so it must be captured live.

label: Audit — Reason
description: Justification, where the change required one.
use_case: Ties probability overrides and stage reversals to their stated reason.

label: Lead
description: The pursuit being analysed.
use_case: §11.2 — win/loss analysis is per pursuit.

label: Outcome
description: Whether the pursuit was won or lost.
use_case: §11.2 — both outcomes are analysed, not just losses.

label: Reason Code
values_note: Same values as Closed Lost Reason Code
description: Structured reason for the outcome.
use_case: §11.2 — makes loss patterns countable rather than anecdotal.

label: Why We Lost
description: Narrative explanation of the loss.
use_case: §11.2 — the first of five questions the playbook mandates.

label: Was It Winnable
description: Whether a different strategy could have changed the outcome.
use_case: §11.2 — separates bad luck from bad execution.

label: What We Would Do Differently
description: The specific process or platform improvement identified.
use_case: §11.2 — the only part of win/loss that changes future behaviour.

label: Who Won
description: The competitor that took the deal.
use_case: §11.2 — feeds the competitive intelligence library.

label: Competitor Solution Type
description: Whether the winner sold a platform or a point solution.
use_case: §11.2 — tests directly whether the platform positioning is landing.

label: Completed By
description: Who performed the analysis.
use_case: §11.2 — accountability for the review being done at all.

label: Completed Date
description: When the analysis was completed.
use_case: §11.2 — required within two weeks of notification for losses above $100K.

label: Category
description: Technical, commercial, contractual, delivery, competitive or geopolitical.
use_case: §10.2 — the six categories the playbook identifies for Astrikos bids.

label: Risk Description
description: The risk itself.
use_case: §10.1 — a named risk can be mitigated; an unnamed one cannot.

label: Probability
description: Likelihood the risk materialises.
use_case: §10.1 — one axis of the response matrix.

label: Impact
description: Severity if the risk materialises.
use_case: §10.1 — the other axis of the response matrix.

label: Required Response
description: Avoid, mitigate, transfer or accept.
use_case: §10.1 — derived from probability and impact; very high on both means do not proceed.

label: Owner
description: Who owns the risk.
use_case: §10.1 — ownership escalates with severity, up to the CEO.

label: Mitigation
description: The mitigation plan.
use_case: §10.1 — high risks require a documented plan in the bid itself.

label: Status
description: Open, mitigated, closed or materialised.
use_case: §10.1 — reviewed at each stage gate.

label: Milestone
description: Which of the eight standard payment milestones this is.
use_case: §8.3 — from contract signing through to handover.

label: % of Value
description: The share of contract value released at this milestone.
use_case: §8.3 — 40 percent sits behind delivery alone, which is why timing matters.

label: Triggering Document
description: The document that releases the payment.
use_case: §8.3 — each milestone has a defined evidence trigger.

label: Milestone Status
description: Not due, due, invoiced or paid.
use_case: §8.2 — drives the cash-flow forecast and credit period measurement.

label: Breach Parameter
description: Which commercial threshold has been exceeded.
use_case: §8.2 — the register of every policy exception on a deal.

label: Policy Value / Actual Value
description: The policy limit against what was actually agreed.
use_case: §8.2 — a breach is only visible if both numbers are held.

label: Breach Approval
description: The approval covering the breach.
use_case: §8.2 — gate G3 requires every breach to carry an approval before Stage 7.

label: Competitor Name
description: The competitor organisation.
use_case: §11.2 — the competitive intelligence library.

label: Competitor Type
description: Platform, point solution, incumbent or low-cost.
use_case: §10.2 — the three competitive threats the playbook names explicitly.

label: Competitor Sectors
description: Where this competitor is typically encountered.
use_case: §11.2 — helps anticipate who will appear on a given tender.

label: Typical Solution
description: What they usually propose.
use_case: §11.2 — feeds the value proposition and objection handling for the bid.
